title: Trillion X
opening: A workflow can produce complete reports while the intended result is still missing. Check the work against its purpose, then check the method when its result or burden calls for it.

labels.review: Check the work and the method
labels.reviewIntro: Select what the evidence says about the result. This choice guides the next inspection; it does not grade a person or prove a method works.
labels.goodResponse: Keep the working method. It does not need a redesign to look sophisticated.
labels.missResponse: Inspect the method’s assumptions and operations, then compare a correction against the purpose.
labels.burdenResponse: Examine which operation creates avoidable burden and whether a simpler arrangement can preserve the useful result.
labels.routeResponse: After any change, inspect both the result and the total burden. Retain an improvement where the next use can find it.
labels.private: This optional note is private practice. The six required course questions are separate.
labels.practiceIntro: Name its purpose, inspect its actual result and burden, and record what evidence would justify a change. The example is illustrative.
labels.sampleLoaded: Illustration loaded. It is not a report of an observed outcome.
labels.length: This full note is over 2,000 characters. Shorten it to save; all of your text stays here.
labels.sourceQuote: Trillion X applies this standard recursively to the work and to the method doing it. If a method repeatedly produces completed records while leaving the intended result absent, examine the method itself. The learner’s ability to use the published lesson remains the test.
labels.noChange: Keep the current method and check again when new evidence or conditions make its result uncertain.

feedback.unavailable: Private saving is unavailable. Your note stays on screen.
feedback.length: Shorten the full note to fit the 2,000-character limit. Your text stays here.
feedback.conflict: This note changed elsewhere. Your answers remain here; compare the saved version before saving again.
feedback.readFailure: The saved note could not be loaded.
feedback.readbackFailure: The save could not be confirmed. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.saveFailure: The save is uncertain. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.retryPending: The earlier save is unresolved. Retry the same note before changing it.

steps.title: Compare the result with its purpose
steps.detail: Use the actual result as evidence. A complete report or list of activities does not substitute for the intended result.

steps.title: Examine the method when needed
steps.detail: If the result is wrong or the burden is unnecessary, inspect the method’s assumptions and operations.

steps.title: Reuse a correction and compare
steps.detail: Compare an applicable correction with a better arrangement. A working simple method needs no redesign for appearance.

steps.title: Apply and inspect again
steps.detail: Check both the output and the total burden after the change.

steps.title: Keep the improvement where future work can find it
steps.detail: Save the supported change with the people who maintain this method so the next use can inherit it.

fields.label: What result is this process meant to produce?
What result have you actually observed?
What time, effort, or other burden does the method add?
What assumption or operation would you inspect or change?
After a change, what result and total burden will you inspect, and where will you keep a useful correction for later use?

example.purpose: Help a learner choose when to use the method.
example.actual: The page has every heading, but the learner still cannot choose when to use it.
example.burden: Adding more headings would increase reading without addressing the missing choice.
example.correction: Compare a short contrast that shows when the method fits with a case where it does not.
example.evidence: Check whether a learner can choose appropriately after using the revision, and whether the added explanation makes the page harder to use. Keep a useful correction with the people who maintain the lesson.

source.assessmentBoundary: Six required open-ended course questions remain separate from this optional private note. No qualified semantic grade or learner outcome is supplied.
